The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, or ANWR, is in northeastern Alaska. It covers part of the Alaska North Slope region. ANWR is the biggest national wildlife refuge in the United States. The office managing it is in Fairbanks. Many animals live there, like polar bears, grizzly bears, black bears, moose, caribou, wolves, eagles, lynx, wolverines, martens, beavers, and birds that migrate. Across the border in Canada are two national parks called Ivvavik and Vuntut.

Hans von Borsody was a German film actor. He was born on September 20, 1929, in Vienna, from a Hungarian descent family with artistic roots. His father, Edvard, was a film director, and his uncle Julius worked as a set designer. His daughter Suzanne became an actress. Borsody moved to Berlin when he was three years old and got German citizenship. He was married four times: to Karin Dittmann, Rosemarie Fendel, Alwy Becker, and Heide Keller.

Very High Frequency (VHF) Omnidirectional Range (VOR) helps airplanes find their position and stay on course. Airplanes get information from fixed ground radio beacons using a receiver unit. VOR works with frequencies between 108.00 to 117.95 MHz in the VHF band. Developed starting in 1937, VOR became the standard air navigation system by 1946 and is used worldwide for both commercial and general aviation. By 2000, about 3,000 VOR stations were operating globally, with around 1,033 in the US; this number decreased to 967 by 2013 as GPS became more popular. A VOR ground station sends signals that rotate 30 times per second and a steady signal at 30 Hz. This helps airplanes find their direction from the beacon relative to magnetic north. Using signals from two different VOR stations, pilots can pinpoint their position. VOR coverage is limited to about 200 miles as it depends on line of sight between transmitter and receiver. Each station sends a VHF signal that includes navigation information, the station’s identifier in Morse code, and sometimes voice messages like station name, flight advisories, or live broadcasts.

The Singapore flag was adopted in 1959, the year Singapore became self-governing within the British Empire. It became the official flag again when Singapore separated from Malaysia on August 9, 1965. Before becoming independent, it was the only state flag in Malaysia with a different width to length ratio. The flag has two colors: red at the top and white below. In the top-left corner is a white crescent moon next to a five-pointed star. These symbols mean that Singapore is a young nation growing stronger, promotes equality among people, and stands for important national values. On water, ships do not use the national flag as their main flag. Instead, they fly a civil ensign with a red background having a white version of the crescent and stars symbol in the middle. Non-military government boats, like coast guard ships, fly a blue state ensign with the national flag in the top-left corner and an eight-pointed compass rose below it. Naval warships use a similar naval ensign but with a white background. There are rules about when and how to fly the Singapore flag. These rules now allow citizens to put the flag on their cars during holidays, and they can also display it at home anytime.

Grandval is a municipality in the Jura Bernois area, which is part of the canton of Bern in Switzerland. It is in the French-speaking region called the Bernese Jura (Jura Bernois). Grandval was also known by its German name "Granfel" or "Granfelden," but people no longer use these names commonly.

The Blossoms are an American girl-group from California. In the 1960s, their most famous members were Darlene Love, Fanita James, and Jean King. The group made its own records but is best known for singing on hit songs. They recorded "He's a Rebel," which Phil Spector credited to The Crystals. The Blossoms provided backing vocals for many big hits from the 1960s. In terms of their importance, The Blossoms were like The Sweet Inspirations on the East Coast and The Andantes for Motown.

Murray was an electoral division in Victoria, Australia. It was in the north of the state near the Murray River, which is the border between Victoria and New South Wales. The town areas included were Shepparton, Echuca, Cobram, Yarrawonga, Boort, and Bridgewater. In 2018, it was renamed Nicholls for use at the 2019 federal election.

Greifswald (also called the University and Hanseatic City of Greifswald in German) is a city in northeastern Germany. It's about equally far from Berlin and Hamburg, Germany’s two largest cities, and is around 80 km (50 miles) from the Polish border. Located in Western Pomerania, Greifswald borders the Baltic Sea and has a small river called Ryck running through it. It is near Germany’s two biggest islands, Rügen and Usedom, and close to three of Germany's national parks. Greifswald became the capital of the new district of Vorpommern-Greifswald after changes in September 2011. Together with Stralsund, Greifswald is one of four main cities in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. As of 2013, its population was about 55,659, including many students and workers at the University of Greifswald. Greifswald attracts international interest because of the university, its biocon valley area, the Nord Stream gas pipeline, and the Wendelstein 7-x nuclear fusion project.

Kraftwerk, which means "power station" in German, is a group formed by Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider in Düsseldorf in 1970. They are known for creating new sounds and being early pioneers of electronic music. Kraftwerk started in West Germany's experimental music scene in the early 1970s and later used lots of machines like synthesizers, drum machines, and vocoders to make their music. They made popular albums such as "Autobahn" (1974), "Trans-Europe Express" (1977), "The Man-Machine" (1978), and "Computer World" (1981). Their music had a special style they called "robot pop," which mixed electronic sounds with catchy tunes, simple arrangements, and repeated beats. They also wore matching suits. Wolfgang Flür left the group in 1987, followed by Karl Bartos in 1990. Florian Schneider left in 2008. Kraftwerk's music has influenced many artists and genres, including synth-pop, hip hop, post-punk, techno, ambient, and club music. In 2014, they received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. They won another Grammy for best dance/electronic album with their live album "3-D The Catalogue" in 2018. As of 2020, the band continues to perform.
